title: S2 P1 foundation: host-persisted test-run transition record, joint transition-and-prompt release prerequisite, and owner acknowledgement, inactive in production until launch provenance and the host route land
outcome: A host-persisted, restart-safe transition record and settlement path for declared test-run transitions exists. Deterministic tests prove it through a test-only verified-provenance input, while production stays inactive: without host-observed launch provenance and positive host-route authority, no owner resume is created and the transition shows a visible blocker. A transition's resume prompt is released only on an exact transition-and-prompt durability conjunction, on every release path including boot. The exact owner can acknowledge a delivered transition through an authenticated boundary, and the UI distinguishes delivered-awaiting-acknowledgement from acknowledged. Launch observation, the route discriminator, mail suppression and production activation stay open in w-6efe's package (iii) and its final integration. No polling, watchdog, timer or new telemetry.
acceptance:
In production, a declared transition creates no owner resume prompt unless it has host-observed launch provenance and positive, immutable host-route authority. Without them it shows a visible Blocked disposition (unverified provenance, or unsupported route) that a rescan does not undo.
- request.json owner metadata never grants authority on its own.
- S1 and legacy runs keep their mailbox route and get no host wake.
- Provenance and route authority can be supplied only through a test-only input that is unavailable outside cfg(test).
Tests show the production blocker, the legacy route unchanged, and the test-only input absent from non-test builds.

The exact owner acknowledges a delivered transition through an authenticated boundary that derives the caller's session identity, never trusting an owner id supplied in a body or path.
- A duplicate acknowledgement is idempotent.
- A wrong or stale owner, or a wrong or stale transition identity, is rejected.
- Delivery and acknowledgement are distinct persisted states. An acknowledgement neither records provider acceptance nor clears a delivery conflict.
- The UI shows a delivered transition as awaiting the owner until it is acknowledged, and as acknowledged afterwards.
Rust and UI tests cover both states and the rejections.
The full gate passes on the exact committed tree.
